open_questions: Transit depths are formally inconsistent (transit_depths p_consistent 2.15184081011347e-07) with epoch -1 depth 1029 ppm vs mean 3770 ppm outlier sigma -4.4; low SNR per transit (refit snr 10.99, only 3 transits with difs 2 near gap) increases scatter uncertainty but signal still requires more monitoring to confirm repeatability.

Duration is short for the target (duration.ratio 0.4491, observed_h 1.25 vs central_h 2.784) implying a significant impact parameter or eccentric orbit; high-resolution photometry and radial velocities would further test against a diluted/blended EB, and centroid_all remains inconclusive with diff_snr 0.6345.

Star is M dwarf with neighbours.plausible_within_1px 1 and could_cause 55, but secondary, shape and on-target stellar density (fit_log_density_ratio 0.7862) disfavour a neighbour EB as best explanation; follow-up to rule out the 17.4 arcsec neighbour is prudent.
dossier.public_summary: The 1.25-hour, 3,793 ppm dips repeat every 11.5 days on a likely M dwarf and have flat bottoms typical of a transit, with no secondary eclipse and a size of about 4 Earth radii. One of the three dips is much shallower and the light curve is noisy, so the depths vary more than expected, and the measured centroid is inconclusive, but the flat shape, small size, and lack of binary signatures make a planet the best explanation; more observations are needed to confirm the cause of the depth scatter and the short duration.

reasons.why: Strongly flat-bottomed (negative v_sigma) favours a planet transit over a grazing V-shaped binary eclipse, despite low impact parameter indicated by fit_b 0.2098.
Implied planet radius is sub-Neptune (rp/R* 0.06506) with positive Gaia radii confirming Rp ~4.15 Re for a small planet, not a stellar eclipsing binary.
No significant secondary at half phase (snr_at_half -1.13) and phase_curve ratio_to_depth 0.08736 with chi2 7.568/9 shows no close-binary phase swing, unlike an EB on the target.
ML scorer rates it as planet-like as the median known planet, supporting planet as best explanation when combined with flat shape, no secondary and small size.

Odd-even difference below strong threshold (depth_ratio 1.7) and explained by single shallow outlier does not outweigh positive planet evidence; depth scatter is better explained by transit_depths inconsistency than by 23-d binary.
